From 93e3bce6287e1fb3e60d3324ed08555b5bbafa89 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2015 09:25:00 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] vfs: Remove incorrect debugging WARN in prepend_path

The warning message in prepend_path is unclear and outdated.  It was
added as a warning that the mechanism for generating names of pseudo
files had been removed from prepend_path and d_dname should be used
instead.  Unfortunately the warning reads like a general warning,
making it unclear what to do with it.

Remove the warning.  The transition it was added to warn about is long
over, and I added code several years ago which in rare cases causes
the warning to fire on legitimate code, and the warning is now firing
and scaring people for no good reason.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Ivan Delalande <colona@arista.com>
Reported-by: Omar Sandoval <osandov@osandov.com>
Fixes: f48cfddc6729e ("vfs: In d_path don't call d_dname on a mount point")
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>

diff --git a/fs/dcache.c b/fs/dcache.c
index 656ce522a218..615dfc2aa752 100644
--- a/fs/dcache.c
+++ b/fs/dcache.c
@@ -2927,17 +2927,6 @@ static int prepend_path(const struct path *path,
 				vfsmnt = &mnt->mnt;
 				continue;
 			}
-			/*
-			 * Filesystems needing to implement special "root names"
-			 * should do so with ->d_dname()
-			 */
-			if (IS_ROOT(dentry) &&
-			   (dentry->d_name.len != 1 ||
-			    dentry->d_name.name[0] != '/')) {
-				WARN(1, "Root dentry has weird name <%.*s>\n",
-				     (int) dentry->d_name.len,
-				     dentry->d_name.name);
-			}
 			if (!error)
 				error = is_mounted(vfsmnt) ? 1 : 2;
 			break;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/dcache.c`**
- The patch removes a block of code that contains a warning message in the `prepend_path` function. This warning was intended to alert developers about the use of the `d_dname` function for generating names of pseudo files, particularly when dealing with root directory entries that have unusual names.
- The specific warning that was removed checks if a directory entry (`dentry`) is a root and whether its name is not just a single '/' character. If the conditions were met, it would trigger a warning message.

### Relationships
- The removal of the warning is related to the historical context of the code, as the warning was deemed outdated and unclear. It was originally added to address a transition in the codebase regarding how names for pseudo files were generated. However, since the transition has long been completed, the warning was no longer relevant and was causing confusion among developers.
- The patch also references a previous commit (`f48cfddc6729e`) that indicates the context in which the warning was added, highlighting that the warning was firing incorrectly in some legitimate cases due to changes made in the code several years prior. Thus, the removal of the warning is a corrective action to improve code clarity and reduce unnecessary alerts.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (IS_ROOT(dentry) &&
   (dentry->d_name.len != 1 ||
    dentry->d_name.name[0] != '/')) {
    WARN(1, "Root dentry has weird name <%.*s>\n",
         (int) dentry->d_name.len,
         dentry->d_name.name);
}
```
Reason:
The warning was triggered when the `dentry` was a root directory but had a name that was not just a single forward slash. This condition was meant to catch unusual cases, but since the transition to using `d_dname` was long over, the warning became irrelevant and started to fire in legitimate scenarios, causing confusion among developers.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-            /*
-             * Filesystems needing to implement special "root names"
-             * should do so with ->d_dname()
-             */
-            if (IS_ROOT(dentry) &&
-               (dentry->d_name.len != 1 ||
-                dentry->d_name.name[0] != '/')) {
-                WARN(1, "Root dentry has weird name <%.*s>\n",
-                     (int) dentry->d_name.len,
-                     dentry->d_name.name);
-            }
```
Reason:
The removal of the outdated warning code eliminates the confusion it caused, as it was no longer relevant to the current implementation. By removing this code, the function `prepend_path` no longer incorrectly warns developers about legitimate root directory names, thus improving clarity and reducing unnecessary alarm.
